_comment: Serenza's villagers (docs/locations/cliffs.md): routines, greetings, topics and gifts.

npcs.name: Marta Bonanni
npcs.title: Back from the agency in Toriano

lines: Serenza: where Easter comes up the hill. That's the slogan now. Nonno hates it. He's using it.
The hiking club booked again for next year. I faxed them the confirmation twice, to be sure.
Geometra! I've got a slogan for you: 'Serenza. It's Steep. It's Worth It.' No? I'm workshopping it.
Nonno's speaking to me again. Mostly to say I'm wrong. That's progress.
My mobile has one bar of signal up by the sanctuary. One bar! I'm basically in Toriano.
You're the Geometra! Off the 8:10, right on time. Well, eleven minutes late. On time for Serenza.

sleepy: Zzz… Serenza… bottled sunshine… no… terraced sunshine…

topics.label: Why did you write to the province?
lines: Because Nonno wouldn't. The cooperative votes in April whether to close. Twelve growers, average age seventy-four.
If the terraces go back to brambles, the walls fall, the hill slides, and Serenza ends up in the harbour. Slowly. Then quickly.
So I wrote. On agency letterhead. I may have implied the agency was involved. The agency was not involved.

topics.label: What did you do in Toriano?
lines: Advertising. Biscuits, mostly. I wrote 'Crunchy on Monday, crunchy on Friday'. You've heard it. Everyone's heard it.
Then my grandmother died and I came back for the funeral, and stayed for the terraces. The biscuits can crunch without me.

topics.label: How do you get on with Settimio?
lines: We argue every day. Breakfast, lunch, the bar in the evening. It's how we say good morning.
He thinks a fax machine is the devil's typewriter. I think he's the most stubborn man on the Riviera. We're both right.

gifts.line: Two bottles of the sweet wine. Unlabelled. For now. I have designs.

npcs.name: Presidente Settimio "Gerla" Crovara
npcs.title: President of the growers' cooperative

lines: The cooperative stays open. I voted for it. Don't tell Marta I enjoyed it.
Sixty years I've carried that basket up these steps. Now I've got company. It's annoying. It's good.
The wall's holding. I went and kicked it this morning. It'll do. For now.
The lizards are on your stones. Lizards don't sit on bad walls.
Hm. The Geometra. Still here.
Mind where you step. That's a vine, not a weed.
My granddaughter writes to the province. I write to nobody. The terraces don't read.
Who are you? The Geometra? Marta's doing, I suppose. Hm.

sleepy: Zzz… the wall under W4… hold, you… hold…

topics.label: Why do they call you Gerla?
lines: Gerla. The basket on your back. Grapes down, manure up. Every day since I was nine.
Nobody else carries one now. They've got the monorail, when it runs. I've got knees. Mine still run.

topics.label: How do you build a dry-stone wall?
lines: No mortar. Just stones, the right way round. Big ones at the bottom, long side into the hill, and lean it back a little.
Every stone has one place it wants to sit. You find it. If you don't, the wall tells you. In winter. All over the vines.

topics.label: What's the vote about?
lines: Twelve of us left. Average age seventy-four, and that's with Marta lowering it.
In April we vote whether to sell the cellar and let the terraces go. I've voted no for thirty years. Nobody's ever asked twice.

gifts.line: Two vine cuttings. From the old Bosco on E2. Don't drown them.
My spare hat. Fifty summers. The holes are where the sun gets in. Wear it on the terraces.

npcs.name: Mario "Trenin" Cozzani
npcs.title: Perito meccanico, keeper of the monorail

lines: Zia Pina's been up and down six times today. She's never been happier. She's a cart.
Listen to that engine. Brrrrrr-tak. That's a contented motor, that is.
Geometra! Come in, mind the sump. Zia Pina, say hello. She doesn't. She's shy.
Seven carts, seven aunts. I'm out of aunts. The next cart will have to be an uncle.
Oh! A visitor. Hello. Don't touch the red one, she bites.

topics.label: What's the monorail?
lines: One rail, up the hill, and a little cart with an engine that sits on it like a hen. You load the cart at the bottom and it climbs.
Every terrace on the coast had one once. Grapes down, stakes up. Without it you need a gerla. And knees like the Presidente's.

topics.label: Why are the carts named after aunts?
lines: Zia Pina, Zia Rosa, Zia Carmela… My mother had six sisters and a cousin she counted as one.
They all climbed these terraces with baskets. Now the carts do it for them. It seemed only fair.

topics.label: Why do they call you Trenin?
lines: Trenin. Little train. Because when I was six I made engine noises all the way up the steps. I still do. Quietly.

gifts.line: Spare parts. Clean ones. Well, cleaner.

npcs.name: Don Aurelio Natale
npcs.title: Priest of the church on the rocks

lines: Fourteen degrees this morning! Bracing. Come in one day. No? One day.
The sea's cold, the Lord is warm, and the towel is in between.
Good morning, Geometra. Or afternoon. On the rocks I lose track. The sea doesn't keep hours.
The ship paintings in the church were all left by sailors who came home. The sea painted the rest.
Welcome! You've come to the right village. It's the only one between those two tunnels.

sleepy: Zzz… et cum spiritu… brrr, cold this morning…

topics.label: You swim every morning?
lines: Every morning of the year. Christmas, Epiphany, the day of the storm in '87. The sea and I have an arrangement.
There was an iron ladder down the rocks. It rusted away last winter. Now I climb in like a crab and out like a seal.

topics.label: What happens at Easter?
lines: The procession! From the church on the rocks, up the main street, under the arch, through the terraces and up to the sanctuary.
Every grower walks behind the statue. Fewer every year. And the mule path's broken in the gully. The old ladies can't climb that.

topics.label: Who painted the ships in the church?
lines: Sailors who survived a storm, mostly. A promise to the Madonna: get me home and I'll paint you my ship.
Capo Horn has promised me one eleven times. Or fourteen. It depends who's listening.

gifts.line: Focaccia from Nunzia. Blessed, so it doesn't count as gluttony.

npcs.name: Capitano Giacomo "Capo Horn" Rollandi
npcs.title: Retired merchant captain

lines: Look at them, riding at their moorings. Like the Pacific Fleet. A very small Pacific Fleet.
Did I ever tell you about Cape Horn? The fourth time? No? Sit down.
Ahoy, Geometra! Mind the nets. They've been mended since Tuesday and they've only got worse.
Eleven times round Cape Horn. Or fourteen. Once you've done it eleven times you stop counting properly.
Ahoy there! New face on the cliff. Welcome aboard. Well, ashore.

sleepy: Zzz… fifty-six degrees south… hard to starboard… zzz…

topics.label: Why Capo Horn?
lines: Cape Horn. The bottom of the world. Waves like apartment blocks and an albatross for every one.
I've rounded it eleven times. Or fourteen. The other three were in a dream, but a very wet one.

topics.label: Why are the boats in the street?
lines: Every winter the village hauls its boats up out of the storms. Every spring we slide them back down the slipway.
Only the slipway crumbled. So the boats are in the main street, and I'm mending nets beside them, and the street is mostly boat.

topics.label: Do you miss the sea?
lines: It's right there. I look at it every day. It looks back. We have an understanding: I don't go out, and it doesn't come in.

gifts.line: Salted anchovies. My mother's recipe. My mother's jar, too.

npcs.name: Nunzia Lercari
npcs.title: Runs the bar on the harbour square

lines: The hiking club wrote in the guest book. Eight pages. One each. Very neat handwriting. Schoolteachers.
Coffee? I've got a new tablecloth and I'm dying to spill something on it.
Geometra! Coffee? Of course coffee. Sit. You look tired. It's the steps. Everyone looks tired here.
Did you hear? No? Sit down, I'll tell you. Don't tell anyone I told you.
Eleven days to my first Easter guests. Twelve. I counted wrong. I'll count again.
A new face! Sit, sit. I'm Nunzia. This is the bar. That's the payphone. That's Marta's fax. It's very loud.

sleepy: Zzz… table four… two coffees and a focaccia… zzz…

topics.label: Who's coming for Easter?
lines: A hiking club! From Toriano! Eight retired schoolteachers in matching red anoraks. They wrote on headed paper.
My first guests in the rooms upstairs since 1991. I've aired the mattresses twice. I'll do it again.

topics.label: Is that the village's only phone?
lines: The payphone. The only one between the tunnels. Everybody's business goes through that phone, and I'm standing right next to it.
I don't listen. I just hear. There's a difference, and I'll explain it to you sometime.

topics.label: What's the Easter pie?
lines: Torta di erbe. Wild greens off the terraces, borage, eggs, a little cheese, and pastry so thin you can read the paper through it.
My grandmother made it with greens from every terrace. Now there are brambles where the greens were.

gifts.line: Lemon cake, from the bottom shelf. The good shelf. Don't tell the guests.

lines: I missed the 21:40 again. The shelter is very comfortable. I have filed a note of thanks.
Good morning. I have slept in a structure within the regulations. A first.
Good day. Ragionier Sturlese, comune of the next town. I have forms. I always have forms.
Dry stone only. Slate roofs only. Nothing taller than the bell tower. I don't make the rules. I photocopy them.
If you'll excuse me, the 17:52 waits for no clerk. Neither does the 21:40, as it happens.
You must be the Geometra. I have a form for that. Several.

topics.label: What are the landscape rules?
lines: Three rules, Geometra. Dry stone walls only. Slate roofs only. Nothing taller than the bell tower.
I write them on every brief. Then I stamp the permit anyway. The rules are the rules, but the stamp is the stamp.

topics.label: Do you really miss the last train?
lines: One day in three. It's statistically consistent. The 21:40 leaves at 21:40 and I arrive at 21:41.
I have run for it in these shoes four hundred and twelve times. I keep a record. It's very thorough.

topics.label: What's in the briefcase?
lines: Forms, stamps, an ink pad, a sandwich and a timetable. In that order. The sandwich moves up when I'm hungry.

gifts.line: A refund. You overpaid a stamp duty you didn't owe. I noticed. I always notice.
